What Is GTA VI Trying to Say About the Manosphere?

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1894 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gq

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, what’s a man allowed to like these days?
  • We asked a physical therapist, developers, and other gaming obsessives for the best tips to help you highjack garbage trucks in Leonida for as long as humanly possible.
  • In a recent development, grand Theft Auto VI, these men assert, is emasculating because it asks players to role-play a man that respects his partner and do mundane tasks she would appreciate, like repaint their bedroom or get her a nice necklace.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, what’s a man allowed to like these days? Not the Super Bowl, or Christopher Nolan movies, it seems, each of them guilty of sins against masculinity. Now there is a new offender: Grand Theft Auto VI. Over one brief weekend, Rockstar’s long-in-the-works, exorbitantly expensive opus has given us a rare monocultural moment and elicited a wounded reaction from a slice of gamers steeped in the streams and podcasts of right-wing figures like Steven Crowder, Zack “Asmongold” Hoyt, and Braden Eric “Clavicular” Peters.

We asked a physical therapist, developers, and other gaming obsessives for the best tips to help you highjack garbage trucks in Leonida for as long as humanly possible.

In a recent development, grand Theft Auto VI, these men assert, is emasculating because it asks players to role-play a man that respects his partner and do mundane tasks she would appreciate, like repaint their bedroom or get her a nice necklace. For others, it is less that the game is offensively woke and more that its wokeness is getting in the way of their fun. “You can’t kiss anyone other than your strong female Latina partner,” complains Crowder, his cohosts all lamenting that video games ought to be a vehicle for their every base fantasy. These men object to what they see as politics encroaching on what they think ought to be a politics-free space, “shut up and dribble” but for violent video games. But there’s a delicious irony to this because the game genuinely has a bone to pick with these unfortunate figureheads of the manosphere.

The manosphere, it should be noted, is a (shitty) state of mind. Less a formal designation than a collection of people who promote similar sexist, racist, and/or fascist ideals, a loose web of podcasters, streamers, and influencers who all preach a gospel of grievance in which men are victims of women withholding sex, liberals withholding power, and other men for not performing masculinity correctly. They can run the gamut from disgraced influencer Andrew Tate (right now in jail awaiting trial for a litany of alleged crimes) to the comedians and podcasters orbiting Joe Rogan’s massive audience. But they all have one thing in common: These men and the people who pay rapt attention to them are the targets of Grand Theft Auto VI’s satire.

According to recent reports, some background here: While yes, Grand Theft Auto VI casts players as modern Bonnie and Clyde Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos, their story is only one reason to play the game. Another is the incredibly dense setting of Leonida, a feverish and astonishingly lifelike take on Florida, chock-full of weirdos and wildlife to take in. Layered on top of that is a whole media ecosystem: a fake Instagram to scroll named Snapmatic, a news feed app, a suite of radio stations with robust programming including two talk radio stations, three TV networks with entire shows, and magazines and books you can read in excerpts.

Recent findings suggest that it’s in all this background material that Grand Theft Auto VI really tears into the modern grievance grift of the manosphere. The game’s decade-plus gestation means it’s had a lot of time to amass a shooting gallery of noxious conservative male influencers that the algorithm has elevated and buried, ranging from flat-earth conspiracy theorists to MAHA-adjacent cronies. On the Weazel TV network, you can find these views as the punchline of entire Adult Swim–esque cartoons like Right Wing, about a patriotic superhero horrified to learn that a straight pride parade has been transformed by a gay superhero called the Flamer. “All these years suppressing who I was, but now I’m free!” shouts Right Wing’s colleague Great Uncle Sam after the Flamer has liberated him. “Isn’t that what America is all about?” “No,” Right Wing retorts. “America is about guns, and lots of them!”.

According to recent reports, scroll through Snapmatic, and you can find a clear analogue of Liver King—the content creator who promoted an “ancestral lifestyle” that involved consuming raw animal organs—posting under @paleoprimal. In one of his faux influencer videos, he advises his followers to “start beating your meat,” before dropkicking a hunk of raw flesh. “I don’t eat anything unless I’ve conquered it first.” Ashes of Glory, a sendup of historical war fiction that sits by Jason’s bed, is drowning in overly reverent prose that also happens to note that its war heroes are psychopaths. One passage: “'You’ve been charged with murdering civilians, violating every law known to God and man, calling your enemies rude names, and uncontrollable teabagging,’ remarked the General. 'Which is exactly why we need your help.’”.

A lot of these blows are glancing, more about attacking attitudes than people, give or take a Liver King. But turn the in-game radio dial to WKTT, Grand Theft Auto VI’s conservative talk radio station, and the targets sharpen. Hosts Richard Bastion (Jason Sudeikis) and Dominic “The Brick” Brizzolato (Stavros Halkias) do pastiches of Alex Jones and Nick Fuentes, spouting racist and sexist takes. Ponytails are “the hairstyle of someone who’s about to suck your dick,” per Brizzolato, who also maintains local football team the Manatees have problems to do with “culture” and “not race.” Every so often they are undercut by callers who ask how performance-enhancing drugs and hair implants don’t count as gender-affirming care. Of the many items they hawk—Flaming O’s snacks, Sprunk soda, and Patriot beer—the most absurd and on-the-nose is a special playing card set with “no queens.”.

In its blunt re-creation of the conservative male media ecosystem, Grand Theft Auto VI plainly states what Rockstar thinks of these guys: They’re really fucking stupid. They are stupid in ways that are true to life and moronic in ways that Rockstar exaggerates, but only just so. They drive home this point by underlining the pathetic loneliness subtextual in all these real-life broadcasts, with Richard Bastion asserting that he doesn’t have friends but is building “a fraternity with a mission to save America” and that friends “let you down” and “tell the papers that your wife sleeps in a separate bed and sometimes house.”.

After 13 years, and a budget rumored to rival that of Dubai’s Burj Khalifa skyscraper, the new Grand Theft Auto is finally here. Our critic's verdict? It's a tour de force that reimagines what a video game can be.

Industry observers note that the message hits cleaner than past iterations of the game not because Grand Theft Auto VI is any less lowbrow than before—it is still awash in dick jokes, memes about shitting your pants, and South Park–esque lambasting of White America—but because this more richly detailed, lifelike version of Grand Theft Auto means the cartoonish aspects stand out all the more. What’s a joke and what is not is clearer than it has ever been.

Recent findings suggest that despite the protests from fans who say the latest iteration of Grand Theft Auto betrays the spirit of the franchise, there was always evidence that the game hated these hypermasculinity-obsessed tryhards, even before they had a manosphere to inhabit. While early games in the series did not have much in the way of plot or characters, they were tongue-in-cheek caricatures of gangster epics and the ambitions of men within them, a touch of arch Scottish humor (Rockstar’s lead Grand Theft Auto team is based in Edinburgh) keeping them from being sincere homages.

Sources indicate that nearly 20 years ago in Grand Theft Auto IV—a series turning point, where the games started to have stories with intentional thematic interests—Rockstar Games incessantly lambasted the pursuit of the hypermasculine. Its protagonist Niko Bellic served as a stoic counterpoint to many of the jacked-up weirdos of the faux New York dubbed Liberty City, arriving in the United States during the game’s opening credits with nothing but the clothes on his back and his cousin Roman’s lies about his own success in his ear. Through Niko’s journey, Grand Theft Auto IV posed the arguments that this country’s obsession with the unfettered pursuit of power and wealth makes people unwell and that culture afflicts men in ways that render them uniquely delusional. It gives his cousin Roman a fantasy of a success that will never come, causing him to submit to the intimidations of two-bit enforcers. It makes men like Brucie Kibbutz, a supplement-obsessed fitness freak, deny his own obvious interest in men in favor of a nonstop stream of homophobic jokes and crude sexual banter. It makes Niko, a soldier who thought he was escaping his criminal past, find himself immediately becoming a different kind of criminal at the behest of men who believe the world is theirs to take. And that’s just in the first few hours.

Grand Theft Auto IV’s skewering came at the expense of others—namely the women and queer people who are the butt of nearly every joke in the game. Seven years later, Grand Theft Auto V would course-correct by being hateful to everyone in its fictional version of Los Angeles: the acai-and-granola liberals and the asshole conservatives alike. It mires itself in the desperation of male entitlement, as three characters—the middle-aged Michael De Santa, the young striver Franklin Clinton, and Trevor Philips, the lewd loose cannon—adjust poorly to a world they cannot dominate. De Santa, arguably the protagonist of the three characters the player can inhabit, sees the world as out to emasculate him, either through his wife’s affair, his deadbeat son, or his daughter, who he must rescue from TV producers that he assumes are predatory. Michael’s world is much simpler when he’s holding a gun, and Grand Theft Auto V is eager to get one in his hands. In this, it feels like the game wants you to agree: Isn’t this more fun than dealing with all that? And it is, because Rockstar made it that way.

It has been revealed that yes, there are missions. But have you seen the kicks?

Recent findings suggest that there has always been a have-it-both-ways nature to Grand Theft Auto’s satire. Rockstar is happy to facilitate the same American male id it’s lampooning, and the staggering number of copies sold suggests that even conservative commentators out there appealing to incel logic are logging right onto their PlayStations the moment they stop posting. But despite what critics may claim to their audiences, Grand Theft Auto VI’s manosphere parodies are not a huge departure for the series, because the problems with toxic masculinity remain woefully consistent, as do the grifters who seek to profit from it. Insecurity is both a significant business and a renewable energy source.

In a recent development, what’s left out of all these complaints about Grand Theft Auto VI being a game where you embody a simp man is that you do not have to do any of the loving behavior these clowns rail against in the video game. You can ignore Lucia when playing as Jason, let your relationship grow distant and decay. You can leave the walls unpainted, never pick up flowers or groceries, not press the button to hold Lucia’s hand, keep your distance on the dance floor. The game just makes clear what the real world does not: That’s a good way to end up alone. And that’s the one thing the parodied blowhards of GTA VI’s in-game manosphere broadcast loud and clear: that they’re alone.

The 7 Most Common Mistakes Home Cooks Make When Cooking Mashed Potatoes

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (622 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Delish

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that in a traditional Thanksgiving meal, mashed potatoes are a seemingly simple side dish that does a lot of heavy lifting.
  • Mashed potatoes prove you can transform even the humblest ingredients into something magical.
  • In a recent development, thankfully, those mistakes are 100% avoidable.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that in a traditional Thanksgiving meal, mashed potatoes are a seemingly simple side dish that does a lot of heavy lifting. They're the perfect vessel for a puddle of gravy, and they’re a creamy complement to everything else on your plate—yes, even your aunt's questionable green bean casserole.

Mashed potatoes prove you can transform even the humblest ingredients into something magical. And yet, we've all somehow still eaten bad ones. With a recipe this basic, even the smallest mistakes have nowhere to hide.

In a recent development, thankfully, those mistakes are 100% avoidable. We rounded up the most common ways to mess up mashed potatoes so that yours turn out as delicious as possible this holiday season.

In a recent development, it doesn’t matter if you cut your potatoes into a fine dice or rough chunks. Whatever size you pick, stick with it. Making sure your potato pieces are roughly the same size will help them all cook at the same rate. If your knife work is haphazard, you may end up with some pieces that are perfectly cooked, others that are waterlogged and mushy, and some that are still firm in the center.

Like pasta, potatoes need a good amount of seasoning to really shine—which is why salting the cooking water is so important. You can be generous with the salt, since much of it stays in the water and ends up going down the drain. When you start seasoning early in the cooking process, it’s easier to build flavor and adjust as you go.

It has been revealed that in the hustle of cooking all of your Thanksgiving dishes, you may be tempted to boil your potatoes ahead of time and mash them later in the day. But it’s always better to work with potatoes while they’re still hot and easier to mash. Waiting until they’re cool will likely require far more elbow grease—and you’ll still end up with uneven chunks.

Industry observers note that A smooth, creamy mash is the height of decadence. To make sure the potatoes are lump-free, some people may reach for a blender—but this is one of the most consequential mistakes you can make. Potatoes are naturally starchy, and the more you work them, the more starch gets released from their cell walls. Breaking out the blender may be well-intentioned, but it can leave you with potatoes that are gummy and gluey. Instead, opt for the right tool, like a hand masher, food mill, or potato ricer.

Sources indicate that another vital thing to consider is that potato starches continue absorbing moisture as mashed potatoes sit. They can soak up the milk you’ve added, leaving your potatoes dry and dense. Don’t be afraid to add more liquid—or at least keep some extra on hand to loosen up your mash before serving.

Anthony Bourdain famously pointed to generous amounts of salt and butter as part of what makes restaurant food taste so good. That’s especially true for mashed potatoes. You may be scared to add more than a light sprinkle of salt, but don’t forget to taste and adjust the seasoning before serving. A little extra salt can make all the difference for your Thanksgiving dinner.

It has been revealed that whether you’re feeding your immediate family or a small army, you should always make a major batch of mashed potatoes. This side is one of the most popular components of a Thanksgiving menu, so it never hurts to make extra. It’s also one of the most versatile dishes for repurposing leftovers. You can transform them into gnocchi, shepherd’s pie, or crispy fried croquettes. It may require more mashing in the moment, but your future self will thank you.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In the midst of a rich meal, something fresh and acidic keeps your taste buds awake. Where lettuce splashed with vinaigrette can feel like an afterthought, a juicy, savory-slanting pear salad is worth making room for on a plate full of turkey and cornbread. This is the antithesis of the haphazardly chunked together fruit salads you find at the supermarket for a brunch or dessert spread. Keep the focus on crisp-tart pears—apples also work—and it’s a welcome accompaniment to the other hearty dishes. Sliced razor-thin (use a mandoline) and fanned out on a platter, the fruit acts as an edible canvas for wisps of cheese and clusters of honey-roasted seeds. Leftovers (if you have any, of course) are delightful spooned over a well-toasted and buttered slice of multigrain bread the next day.

Sources indicate that pick firm green pears (Bartlett and Anjou are fair game; use Asian pears in a pinch) to ensure they hold their shape once sliced—even a little underripe is better than slightly over. After slicing, have a taste: If they are very tart, add 1 tsp. honey to the dressing; if fairly sweet, skip it.

For more Thanksgiving recipes, tips, menus, and inspiration, head to our 2026 Thanksgiving Hub.

According to recent reports, preheat oven to 325°. Whisk 3 Tbsp. honey, 1 tsp. garlic powder, ½ tsp. freshly ground pepper, 3 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil, and ¾ tsp. Diamond Crystal or ½ tsp. Morton kosher salt in a large bowl to combine. Add 1 cup raw sunflower seeds, pumpkin seeds (pepitas), and/or coarsely crushed raw nuts (such as walnuts, almonds, and/or hazelnuts) and stir to coat. Spread out in a single layer on a parchment-lined rimmed baking sheet; reserve bowl.

It has been revealed that bake seed mixture until golden brown, 12–14 minutes. (Honey mixture will puff up a bit but will deflate when you stir.) Toss honey-roasted seeds, then let cool. Toss again just to break up.

Recent findings suggest that whisk 3 Tbsp. fresh lemon juice, 1 tsp. Dijon mustard, a pinch of kosher salt, and remaining 1 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil in reserved bowl. For Geena Meszaros, ‘The Body’ Has Been a Revelation

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1265 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vogue

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that worn by her polarizing character Lisbeth in Netflix’s fresh Catholic school drama The Body, the white crew-neck pullover Meszaros took from set—and is now sporting on our Zoom call—is a key bit of the show’s iconography.
  • It has been revealed that depending on which corner of The Body fandom you find yourself in, Lisbeth is either an innately evil villain or an Ethel Cain–coded antihero.
  • The actress grew up in Calgary, Alberta, a shy kid obsessed with Dakota Fanning who was too scared to ask to go to the bathroom.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Geena Meszaros is in the cat sweatshirt.

It has been revealed that worn by her polarizing character Lisbeth in Netflix’s fresh Catholic school drama The Body, the white crew-neck pullover Meszaros took from set—and is now sporting on our Zoom call—is a key bit of the show’s iconography. The gray kitten’s substantial green eyes gaze slightly upward, a single paw emerging from under her chin. It’s the perfect veneer of innocence; she could either beckon you closer or pounce.

It has been revealed that depending on which corner of The Body fandom you find yourself in, Lisbeth is either an innately evil villain or an Ethel Cain–coded antihero. (The singer-songwriter herself recently weighed in on the show via her Tumblr account: “i fear lisbeth is, in fact, my biological little sister.”) At the beginning of actress-turned-director Quinn Shephard’s series, which is set in 2004, we understand Lisbeth immediately as an outsider. She watches the Lions dance team—headed by queen bee Anya, played by Kristina Bogic—float by in their matching track pants with ill-disguised greed. She moves like someone not totally in control of their limbs. She has no eyebrows. (Well, okay, they’ve just been bleached to the gods.).

The actress grew up in Calgary, Alberta, a shy kid obsessed with Dakota Fanning who was too scared to ask to go to the bathroom. “I was really a nervous, hyper-aware-of-everything child,” Meszaros says. “Then, with my friends, I was always really goofy and would put on weird little personalities.” When I ask her age, she demurs. “I don’t know if the world is ready to know. I’m scared…I play young.” She laughs.

Geena Meszaros as Lisbeth in The Body.

It has been revealed that even over Zoom, it’s obvious from her mix of humor, plaintiveness, and clear self-possession why she was cast as Lisbeth. (“I think I’ve embraced the weird a little bit more outwardly,” she states of her own growth since her teenage years.) She almost decided to be a painter instead of an actress. On her Art by Geena Instagram account, she shares self-portraits and thoughtfully bizarre scenes from real life. (In one, her mom’s Italian greyhound gnaws on a Barbie doll.) While filming The Body, she painted a portrait of herself as a skull with lipstick on. “That was a representation of how I felt while I was filming. I was kind of dead, a little bit ill, but having a great time.”.

The eyebrows both isolate Lisbeth and imbue her with a sort of strange power. (The show’s makeup artists got the look by bleaching them every two weeks. “I was sure I was going to lose my eyebrows, but then when I dyed them back at the end, they were actually so much fuller than they used to be,” Meszaros reports.) By the end of season one, she has the dance team girls in a spiritual chokehold, weaponizing their Catholic guilt against them. But this is no straightforward revenge arc; she is complicated but also deeply cruel, deftly sussing out weakness.

In a recent development, the show’s rapidly growing audience, needless to say, has had its takes—and Meszaros has seen some of the discourse. That Lisbeth comes from a lower-class background, that she has faced more than her fair share of religious trauma at the hands of her mother, that she is essentially the head of her household after the death of her father, don’t totally seem to justify her behavior in the court of online public opinion.

Yet Meszaros has also recognized an key truth about contemporary cultural criticism by way of fandom. “There’s a lot of people that cannot separate the character from the actor, which is fascinating to me,” she says. “I’m like, ‘Yeah, she does some bad things, but she’s not real. Don’t worry. She’s not out there in the world.’” Still, she loves seeing what people come up with in their analysis. “A lot of people think she’s drugging her mom. I’m like, ‘No, that’s not a thing.’ But I do enjoy all the crazy theories anyway. It’s fun, and I’m just happy that people are debating things and that it left them with questions that they’re having fun putting together.”.

Meszaros points to one moment that she herself found tough to take: “That one scene in episode five with Maddie [Shirley Chen], I struggled with that as much as people watching did,” she states, referencing the exorcism of Maddie’s “demon of gluttony”—her eating disorder—which Lisbeth has manipulated her into thinking is a sin. “But I still had that empathy for Lisbeth. I think I had to [in order] to play her, and I do think she’s just gone through so much that you can’t really expect her to be a perfect human being.”.

According to recent reports, “It’s not her most redeemable scene, but I try and tell myself that people like Maddie might be really triggering to Lisbeth because [Lisbeth] used to be really devout, and I think she sees a version of herself that she is still grappling with,” Meszaros continues. “Her mom speaks to her in the way that she’s speaking to Maddie, and it all just comes out in a desperate moment… trauma gets passed down through generations, and I think it can get passed through friendships, too.”.

It has been revealed that meszaros thinks back on her own childhood experiences. “Growing up, I actually used to sort of befriend people who bullied me. I would make myself small if I knew somebody was a threat to me,” she notes. “The way that Lisbeth gets power is by observing the girls and molding herself into them. I really feel like she mimics people…she’s making herself not a threat in such an extreme way. It’s gaining trust, I think. It’s kind of the flip of [my experience] almost, where she starts out small, and then she slowly makes herself bigger.”.

Throughout her season-long quest for belonging, Lisbeth also repeatedly reminds us she’s just a teenage girl finding her way. In one viral scene, she enjoys a particular queer rite of passage: googling “girls kissing” on the internet. (As my lesbian roommate put it, that’s one step before taking an “am I gay?” quiz.) When I ask if Meszaros thinks Lisbeth is on the queer spectrum, she giggles. “I mean, I think everyone is on a queer spectrum.” On the show or in the world? “In the world.”.

Sources indicate that “I think she’s definitely curious,” she indicates. “Her little hookup with Tyler didn’t seem all that buzzy.”.

If the show is renewed for a second season—which seems likely—she’d like to see “what relationship Lisbeth will have with sex. Is it going to be a power thing? Is it going to soften her? I don’t know. But yeah, she could totally be somewhere on the spectrum.”.

It has been revealed that as The Body continues to enjoy its run as the number one show on Netflix, Meszaros is looking forward to actually having a minute to process the success of the show, and her increased visibility. “This role truly was a dream role, and now I have to figure out what my next dream role is going to be,” she says. “I am really excited to just go back and spend time with family and be normal for a little bit.” She also aims to hang out on her sister’s “massive plot of land in the middle of nowhere” this winter: “I think it’d be nice to just go and hibernate. Maybe turn off my phone for a while.”.

It’s getting increasingly difficult to keep up with all the limited-edition tumblers, advent calendars, and seasonal releases that disappear off shelves before you’ve finished your morning coffee. And now IHOP is giving breakfast lovers another reason to make room in their kitchen cabinets.

Delish can exclusively reveal that IHOP is launching its first-ever Collector's Holiday Mug on Monday, November 30, with the mugs being sold at participating restaurants nationwide. It’s also the very first time the pancake chain has ventured into selling merchandise directly to customers—and, as it turns out, the idea has been brewing for quite some time.

It has been revealed that according to Samantha Strong, IHOP’s executive director of brand calendar strategy, the firm has heard from enough coffee-loving customers over the years to realize there was an actual appetite for owning an IHOP mug. “What started as a frequent question has grown into a genuine fan obsession,” she said, and this holiday release is now the company's first attempt to turn that enthusiasm into something people can actually buy.

IHOP says coffee is its second best-selling menu item, which means an awful lot of people have spent their mornings clutching one of those mugs while waiting for breakfast. But before you start planning an entire IHOP-themed kitchen makeover, know that each participating location will have just 24 (yes, only 24!) mugs available. Once they're gone, they’re gone, at least as far as this limited-time release is concerned.

There's certainly no shortage of things to collect this holiday season, but at least this one’s something you can actually put to use while doing some damage to a stack of pancakes.

For more Thanksgiving recipes, tips, menus, and inspiration, head to our 2026 Thanksgiving Hub.

Place a rack in middle of oven; preheat to 325°. Toast ½ cup raw walnuts on a rimmed baking sheet, tossing halfway through, until golden brown, 10–12 minutes.

In a recent development, meanwhile, cook 2 bunches collard greens, ribs and stems removed, leaves cut into 2" pieces, in a large pot of generously salted boiling water until just tender, 9–11 minutes. Using tongs, immediately transfer to a large bowl of ice water and let cool.

Whisk 2 garlic cloves, finely grated, ¼ cup white wine vinegar, 2 Tbsp. Dijon mustard, preferably country-style, ⅓ cup extra-virgin olive oil, ¼ cup (packed) coarsely chopped tarragon, 2 tsp. sugar, and 1 tsp. Diamond Crystal or ½ tsp. Morton kosher salt in a medium bowl to combine. Set dressing aside.

Transfer toasted walnuts to a small bowl and drizzle with remaining 1 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil. Sprinkle with a generous pinch each of sugar and salt and toss to coat. Taste and add more sugar if needed (nuts should be more sweet than salty). Set seasoned walnuts aside.

Drain collard greens and squeeze gently to remove excess water. Transfer to bowl with reserved dressing and toss to coat evenly. Cover and chill at least 15 minutes and up to 2 hours.

It has been revealed that arrange greens in a shallow bowl or on a platter and spoon any dressing remaining in bowl over. Top with seasoned walnuts and tarragon leaves.

Do Ahead: Walnuts can be toasted and dressing can be made 1 day ahead. Store walnuts airtight at room temperature. Cover dressing and chill.

Breaking: The Carnivore Diet Is Peak Protein Extremism. How Healthy Is It Really?

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1376 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gq

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, you know your obsession with protein has gone too far when you’re waiting in line at Erewhon for a raw meat smoothie.
  • Recent findings suggest that eating raw organs is a step too far, but maybe you’ve heard about the benefits of the carnivore diet and you’re curious.
  • It has been revealed that maybe plant-based eating leaves you gassy and unsatisfied.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, you know your obsession with protein has gone too far when you’re waiting in line at Erewhon for a raw meat smoothie. The speciality drink was created by Paul Saladino, who regularly preaches the benefits of following an animal-based diet. If you look inside the blender, you’ll find kefir, beef organs (like liver, heart, kidney, and spleen from Saldino’s Heart & Soil line), and “immunomilk,” which is freeze-dried cow’s colostrum. Yum. Saladino may be an outlier, but he certainly isn’t the only person pushing a meat-heavy diet. Brian Johnson, aka the “liver king,” follows an extreme ancestral carnivore diet, eating a pound of raw liver a day.

Recent findings suggest that eating raw organs is a step too far, but maybe you’ve heard about the benefits of the carnivore diet and you’re curious. According to a 2026 study published in Nutrients, the number of posts about the carnivore diet on Instagram is in the millions—and they didn’t even look at TikTok. Interest surrounding the carnivore diet has shown no signs of slowing down.

It has been revealed that maybe plant-based eating leaves you gassy and unsatisfied. You can’t help that you like wings. Before you take vegetables off the table completely, it’s vital to know what the carnivore diet is and how it impacts health, both short-term and long-term. As experts explain here, it’s not all bad. But there are some important risks to be aware of.

Recent findings suggest that the aforementioned Nutrients study on the carnivore diet explains that there isn’t one standard definition of what the carnivore diet actually is, but generally speaking, it’s a diet where you only eat minimally processed animal foods, including organ meats, fish, seafood, eggs, animal fats, and full-fat dairy. Plant-based foods are eliminated entirely.

While eliminating foods like fruits, vegetables, and whole grains is extreme, Pouria Sefidmooye Azar, PhD, RD, a registered dietitian and assistant professor at the University of Central Arkansas, claims the carnivore diet isn’t all bad. He says that short term, many people lose weight eating this way.

Industry observers note that “Protein is more satiating than carbs and fats, so people following the carnivore diet often stay full for a longer amount of time, which means they reduce their caloric intake,” he states. Logically, it makes sense. If you’re eating foods like beef, chicken, and salmon, you’ll be less likely to dig into the pantry for snacks than if you ate a bowl of noodles.

Industry observers note that dr. Azar indicates it’s important not to conflate weight loss with getting healthier. He says that by eliminating plants, you’re going to miss out on a lot of important nutrients the body needs. You can probably guess the significant one. Yep, fiber. “"If you’re cutting out every plant food, you're not getting fiber or phytonutrients, which are protective compounds found only in plants,” says Chris Vogliano, PhD, RD, a registered dietitian and global food systems expert.

Industry observers note that while you might not suffer any consequences of this immediately, both dietitians say that continuing to eat this way can mess up your digestion. You need fiber for good poops, plain and simple. Dr. Azar notes that we also need fiber to feed the healthy gut bacteria in the microbiome. This is vital for supporting mental health, immune health, and minimizing the risk of chronic diseases and cancers.

According to recent reports, dr. Azar specifically calls out the connection between a high-meat, low-fiber diet and the risk of colorectal cancer. For example, a 2015 Oncology Reviews study shows a connection between red meat consumption and colorectal cancer risk, while a 2026 European Journal of Cancer study called low fiber consumption a major risk factor for colorectal cancer.

Recent findings suggest that considering that men are at increased risk for heart disease (the number one cause of death in the U.S.), it’s important to know how the carnivore diet can impact your cardiovascular health. Spoiler alert: It’s not good. “I would not recommend the carnivore diet as a healthy, long-term eating pattern,” claims Sunny Intwala, MD, MBA, preventive cardiologist and the director of Prevention & Wellness at Northwell Health.

Industry observers note that dr. Intwala explains that this is because meat doesn’t just contain protein; it has a lot of saturated fat too. He says that diets centering around red meat increase LDL cholesterol and blood pressure in a few short weeks. This, he says, can contribute to inflammation and plaque buildup that increases the risk of heart attack and stroke.

According to recent reports, as someone who studies how the way we eat impacts the planet, Dr. Vogliano points out that the carnivore diet is pretty horrible for the environment. “From a food systems lens, a meat-only diet on a global or even national level would carry massive environmental costs from land, water, and greenhouse gas emissions. This is regardless of whether the meat is conventionally raised, organic, or even regenerative. There’s just not enough land to produce that much meat,” he says.

Industry observers note that okay, we need plants. But what about the Brian Johnsons and Paul Salidinos of the world preaching the benefits of eating raw meat? If you are going to eat meat, are there benefits to eating it raw?

Recent findings suggest that both dietitians say no, emphasizing that there is no scientific evidence showing that raw meat is more beneficial in any way than eating cooked meat. “Liver is a nutrient-rich food and a great way to get vitamin A, vitamin B12, folate, and iron. But you can get that from cooked liver; you don’t have to eat it raw,” Dr. Vogliano says. In fact, he emphasizes that eating any meat raw increases the risk of foodborne illnesses like Salmonella and E.coli.

Dr. Azar warns against pulling a Rocky and eating raw eggs either. “The protein in raw eggs is between 50 and 60% digestible. But the protein digestibility in cooked eggs is over 90%,” he says. A study from the ‘90s in The Journal of Nutrition backs this up.

It’s worth noting that this isn’t the same for meat. A 2015 study in the same journal found that the cooking time for meat didn’t impact protein digestibility very much. So while you may get the same amount of digestible protein from raw meat as you would cooked meat, your risk of foodborne illness is greater.

Sources indicate that decades of scientific research make it clear that a plant-free diet is not a healthy diet. If you’re a meat lover, you might be wondering just how much meat you can get away with eating without compromising your health.

Dr. Azar’s advice is this: Meat can still be your primary protein source. Just eat some plants along with it. “If you love meat, you can still eat foods like beef and chicken, but you also need to eat fruits, vegetables, whole grains, and nuts and seeds because there are some nutrients you just can’t get from meat,” he says, adding that only eating meat will lead to nutrient deficiencies.

Dr. Vogliano delivers a dietary message you’ve likely heard many times before: The healthiest diet is a diverse one. “We know from scientific research that the more plant foods our diets consist of, the more insurance we have that we’re getting the nutrients the body needs,” he indicates. Because of this, he advocates for a primarily plant-based diet and only eating meat occasionally.

Different governing bodies have slightly different recommendations when it comes to how much meat you can eat while still maintaining a healthy diet. The American Institute for Cancer Research states to keep red meat under 18 ounces a week, or roughly three portions a week. The American Heart Association doesn’t give a specific serving recommendation for meat, but says to mostly get protein from plants, fish, and seafood.

Dr. Azar emphasizes that there isn’t one universal way of eating that works for everyone. One diet may make one person feel energized and leave someone else feeling exhausted. What is important, he says, is making sure you’re getting all the nutrients your body needs. And what we know for sure is that you can’t do that by just eating meat.

Thanksgiving Cornbread

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, traditionally, cornbread stuffing requires making cornbread, cubing it and letting it dry out, mixing it with stock, eggs, meat, and aromatics, then transforming it into a stuffing (or dressing).
  • Industry observers note that the intentional two-to-one ratio of cornmeal to flour in this cornbread results in a moist, tender crumb that still has enough structure to hold up against the sturdy mix-ins.
  • For more Thanksgiving recipes, tips, menus, and inspiration, head to our 2026 Thanksgiving Hub.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, traditionally, cornbread stuffing requires making cornbread, cubing it and letting it dry out, mixing it with stock, eggs, meat, and aromatics, then transforming it into a stuffing (or dressing). This process produces some truly memorable casseroles, but I have an alternative that streamlines the process without compromising flavor: stuffing cornbread. It still smells enticingly like the classic Thanksgiving side as you set the baking dish on the table. I’ve still packed in a medley of woodsy herbs, sweet onions, vegetal peppers, and savory sausage. And it still slices into lofty servings to perch on your plate next to the sweet potatoes and green beans. It just takes half as long to make.

Industry observers note that the intentional two-to-one ratio of cornmeal to flour in this cornbread results in a moist, tender crumb that still has enough structure to hold up against the sturdy mix-ins. The sugar might seem like a lot, but it balances out the savory sausage and aromatics perfectly.

For more Thanksgiving recipes, tips, menus, and inspiration, head to our 2026 Thanksgiving Hub.

In a recent development, place a rack in middle of oven; preheat to 400°. Line a 13x9" baking pan with parchment paper, leaving generous overhang on long sides. Coat pan and parchment with unsalted butter. Melt ½ cup (1 stick) unsalted butter in a large skillet over medium-low heat, then pour into a small bowl.

Cook 1 green bell pepper, halved, ribs and seeds removed, finely chopped, 1 medium white onion, finely chopped, and 2 celery stalks, finely chopped, in same skillet, stirring occasionally with a wooden spoon, until softened, about 4 minutes. Add 1 lb. spicy and/or sweet Italian sausage, casings removed, and cook, breaking up and stirring occasionally, until browned (it may still be a little raw in the center at this point), about 5 minutes. Remove from heat.

In a recent development, stir together 4 cups (624 g) fine-ground yellow cornmeal, 2 cups (250 g) all-purpose flour, 1 cup (200 g) sugar, 1 Tbsp. plus 1½ tsp. baking powder, 2 tsp. Diamond Crystal or 1¼ tsp. Morton kosher salt, 1 tsp. baking soda, and ¼ cup finely chopped sage, thyme, and/or rosemary in a large bowl. Gradually pour in 3½ cups buttermilk, then melted butter, stirring constantly until combined. Add 4 large eggs one at a time, mixing to incorporate after each addition. Fold in sausage mixture, then scrape batter into prepared pan.

Industry observers note that bake cornbread, rotating pan front to back halfway through, until golden brown and top springs back when gently pressed, 38–45 minutes. Let cool in pan 15 minutes. Using parchment paper overhang, lift cornbread out of pan and transfer to a cutting board. Cut into 12–18 slices; arrange on a platter.

According to recent reports, do Ahead: Cornbread can be baked 4 hours ahead. Store at room temperature; cut just before serving.
